fields.name: Cass Field 01
fields.coverage_basis: 8 of 8 CDL years (2018 to 2025) carry a non-zero class on this field's Crop Sequence Boundary record. This counts years with a class, not the share of the field's area covered by a satellite observation, which is what the Brazil entries' coverage counts.

soil.map_unit: Kindred-Bearden silty clay loams, 0 to 2 percent slopes
soil.method: SDA Tabular post.rest, mapunit joined to muaggatt on mukey, at the field centroid

climate.note: One month at a 4 km cell, read at the field centroid; it is a reanalysis product of the cell, not a gauge at the field.

scenarios.name: Current sequence
scenarios.why: The 2024 and 2025 Crop Sequence Boundary records for this field are Corn and Soybeans, so the current sequence is the pair of crops the field actually grew in its two most recent years.
scenarios.evidence: Eight CDL years, 2018 to 2025, are carried on this field's Crop Sequence Boundary record: 2018 Spring Wheat 2019 Sugarbeets 2020 Spring Wheat 2021 Soybeans 2022 Corn 2023 Soybeans 2024 Corn 2025 Soybeans.
scenarios.benefit: Repeats the pair the field grew in 2024 and 2025, which is the sequence the record shows rather than a proposed one.
scenarios.gap: The record carries no yield, input cost or planting date for either year.
scenarios.risk: The record holds the crop class only, so a late harvest or a wet spring is not visible in it and cannot be ruled out from this evidence.

evidence_rows.value: Kindred-Bearden silty clay loams, 0 to 2 percent slopes (SSURGO map unit 2640846, 1% slope, hydrologic group C, Somewhat poorly drained)

scenarios.name: Spring Wheat → Sugarbeets
scenarios.why: Spring Wheat in 2018 and Sugarbeets in 2019 are adjacent years of this field's own record, so this rotation has already run here.
scenarios.evidence: CDL 2018 is 23 Spring Wheat and CDL 2019 is 41 Sugarbeets on this field.
scenarios.benefit: Adds Spring Wheat, which the current pair does not carry, and it is taken from the field's own history in 2018 and 2019 rather than from a county average.
scenarios.gap: No yield, price or input record is attached to either year of the pair.
scenarios.risk: Sugarbeets appears in only one of the eight years, and the record holds no yield or cost for it, so half of this pair rests on a single observation.

evidence_rows.value: Kindred-Bearden silty clay loams, 0 to 2 percent slopes (SSURGO map unit 2640846, 1% slope, hydrologic group C, Somewhat poorly drained)

scenarios.name: Spring Wheat → Sugarbeets → Soybeans → Corn
scenarios.why: Four crops appear in this field's record between 2018 and 2025; this sequence keeps all four in the order the record shows them.
scenarios.evidence: The distinct crop classes of the eight CDL years are Spring Wheat, Sugarbeets, Soybeans, Corn, in the order they first appear.
scenarios.benefit: Keeps four crops in the rotation, which is the diversity this field has actually carried, not a rotation imported from another field.
scenarios.gap: The record is one class per year, so a double-cropped year counts as one crop and a cover crop is not recorded at all.
scenarios.risk: The order above is the order each crop first appears in the record, not a sequence the field has run in one continuous stretch of years.

evidence_rows.value: Spring Wheat, Sugarbeets, Soybeans, Corn (2018 to 2025)
Kindred-Bearden silty clay loams, 0 to 2 percent slopes (SSURGO map unit 2640846, 1% slope, hydrologic group C, Somewhat poorly drained)

scenarios.why: Four crops appear in this field's record between 2018 and 2025; this sequence keeps all four in the order the record shows them.

scenarios.gap: The record is one class per year, so a double-cropped year counts as one crop and a cover crop is not recorded at all.
scenarios.risk: The four crops do appear in this order from 2020 to 2023, which is one continuous stretch of the record, but that stretch also carries the price and weather of those years and no other.
